newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Amoco stays committed to Romania projects.
newsitem.headline: Amoco stays committed to Romania projects.

text.p: U.S. oil giant Amoco Corp, which earlier this month announced the sale of its retail petrol stations in Romania, said on Thursday it remained committed to other projects in the Balkan country.
"We have key projects on the table now," Michael Adams, president and resident manager of Amoco's Romania subsidiary said in an interview.
He said Amoco had signed separate study agreements with Romania's Petrom RA oil exploration company and Romgaz RA gas utility on projects in the oil and gas sectors.
Petrom plans to upgrade 20 oil deposits under what it said was a project worth "hundreds of millions of dollars".
Romania's gas utility said earlier this year it planned to triple its underground gas storage capacity to some 2.5 billion cubic metres in a $150 million project over five years.
"If these projects prove commercially attractive, Amoco will go forward," Adams said.

Other Amoco plans include building a power station in Romania's capital if it wins a tender bid it submitted last month. The project involves building a plant in Bucharest's northern area, where heating is in short supply, Amoco's Steve Berry said.
"If we win the tender, we could supply heat by the winter of 1999-2000," he added.

Amoco entered its bid along with Electro Invest AB of Sweden in a tender called by Bucharest municipality. Germany's Siemens AG also entered a bid. The municipality is expected to announce the results by end-October.
Amoco has been in Romania since 1992 after winning a concession on an oil block in the Carpathian mountains. It abandoned its first exploratory well there after failing to strike oil.
"We abandoned the well, but we did not abandon the block," Adams said.

Romania, a mature oil and gas producer, has seen its oil output slide over the past 20 years. To capitalise on its potential for new commercial finds the country needs money and technology and foreign investors are seen as a solution.
In April, the country launched a licensing round for 15 onshore and offshore blocks and around 50 local and foreign oil companies have already bought documents for the tender.
Amoco declined to say whether it planned to bid.
